reason: Quota line states 1,000 S3 buckets per sensitive data discovery job and that the quota does not apply to jobs using runtime bucket criteria.
Quota lines state 10,000 custom data identifiers per account and 30 per sensitive data discovery job.
Quote defines a custom data identifier as a regex plus optional character sequences and proximity rule, for particular scenarios, intellectual property or proprietary data.
Opening sentence of What is Amazon Macie matches the claim word for word in substance.
Decision guide row in the data protection offerings table states Macie discovers sensitive data with machine learning and pattern matching and enables automated protection.
The quote supports 5 TB per account per month for discovery jobs only, but not 'by default' or adjustable; that the quota can be raised to 1,000 TB is only in the context sentence after the quote.
Quotes state jobs give deeper targeted analysis with chosen buckets, sampling depth and object criteria, run once or recurring, and incremental daily, weekly or monthly analysis.
Quote defines findings and discovery results and says a result is created for each object a job is configured to analyze, which covers objects without findings or with errors.
FAQ quote states a 30-day free trial of automated sensitive data discovery for all new and existing accounts.
FAQ quote states buckets can be marked in the Macie S3 bucket inventory to be excluded from automated sensitive data discovery.
FAQ quote states 1 GB per month at no cost for sensitive data discovery, not expiring and not bound by the 30-day trial.
FAQ quote states Macie is regional, enabled region by region, with findings across all accounts within each Region.
Quota lines in the sensitive data discovery section state 10 hours to analyze an individual file and that files over the size quota are not analyzed at all.
Quota lines state 1,000 filter rules and suppression rules per account and 15 detection locations per sensitive data finding.
Quote defines a Macie finding as a report of sensitive data in an S3 object or a potential security or privacy issue with an S3 general purpose bucket.
Quote states Macie automatically publishes policy and sensitive data findings to EventBridge and can be configured to also publish them to Security Hub CSPM.
Quotes state automatic enrollment in the 30-day trial on first enable, including member accounts, running 30 consecutive days and not pausable.
Quote states automated discovery object analysis pauses at 150 GB of uncompressed data for a trial account and resumes after the trial ends.

The quote supports only that jobs are excluded and that jobs over 1 GB incur charges; that the trial covers preventative control monitoring and automated discovery is not in the quote, and the page adds a condition for automated discovery (Macie administrator or standalone account).
Pricing quote under the free trial heading states up to 150GB inspected per account, 30 days of bucket inventory and monitoring, and the trial for each new account even in multi-account setups.
Quotes list the three pricing dimensions and possible extra costs for S3 data retrieval and customer managed KMS keys used to decrypt objects.
Quotes support the credentials and financial examples and the PHI and PII categories, but the 'personal information' category and the passport number example appear only in context, not in any quote.
Quota lines state 1,000 member accounts by invitation and 10,000 through AWS Organizations.
Quote states Macie does not analyze data in images, audio, video or other multimedia content.

Quotes support the two ways (Organizations or invitations) and that with Organizations the administrator can enable Macie for members; that the administrator can review member buckets and policy findings and inspect them is only in the context, not in any quote.
Doc-history row dated June 30, 2023 states a delegated Macie administrator can now manage Macie for up to 10,000 accounts.
Quotes state Macie generates a finding for a potential issue such as a bucket becoming publicly accessible, and that such a finding is a policy finding.
Quote states Macie stores policy findings for 90 days.
Doc-history row dated December 6, 2024 states preventative control monitoring for up to 10,000 S3 general purpose buckets per account.
Pricing quote lists the same three charging dimensions.
Quote states Macie integration with EventBridge and Security Hub CSPM is used to monitor, process and remediate findings with other services and systems.
The quote supports 90-day storage and the KMS-encrypted S3 repository for long-term retention, but not 'per Region'; the per-Region scope is in a later paragraph of the page that no quote holds.
Quotes state Macie inventories S3 general purpose buckets, evaluates and monitors them for security and access control, and discovers and reports sensitive data stored in S3.
SRA quote states the Macie service-linked role can be added as a key user of a customer managed KMS key so Macie can scan the data.
SRA quote states Macie is optimized for S3 and data such as RDS or Aurora snapshot exports and exported DynamoDB tables can be moved to S3 for evaluation.

SRA quote states the delegated administrator can enable or suspend Macie, create jobs for member buckets and view all policy findings, while sensitive data findings are visible only to the job creator account.

Quotes support the Glacier Deep Archive, Express One Zone and directory bucket exclusions and Glacier Instant Retrieval support; S3 Standard, Standard-IA, One Zone-IA and Intelligent-Tiering appear only in context, not as quoted value lines.
Quote states the Usage page shows remaining free trial days and a breakdown of estimated usage costs in USD.
Doc-history row dated July 2, 2025 states Macie supports VPC interface endpoints and endpoint policies in all Regions where it is available.
Quotes state cross-Region aggregation adds no cost, aggregates only from Regions where Security Hub CSPM is enabled, and does not enable it automatically.
